text: I cannot recommend this class enough!!! A great intro to salsa/bachata taught by the kindest instructor. I had a blast learning with everyone. This was such a fun and welcoming experience that’s allowed me to connect to my roots while making new connections. Excited to continue growing and learning with this newfound community. Thank you Michelle and Pat for all your hard work and hosting this safe space for the queer community <3
author: Marisol

text: I'm definitely not the best dancer but Michelle was so welcoming, I felt more confident and capable than I'd ever have expected! The progression of routine was also quite nice - a good balance of challenge and ease. Gracias a ti Michelle!
author: Luke

text: Michelle’s passion for dance and genuine care for every student create an incredibly welcoming environment. I highly recommend her to anyone seeking an inspiring instructor and a safe space to be yourself.
author: Paul

text: I'm so glad I found this group! I love to dance but dance classes (specially Latin dances) are very "men lead and women follow" so I never felt comfortable enough with trying out leading until now. Michelle is a great teacher and the vibes are just so chill and welcoming. Also, having a progression of classes helped to solidify the content in a way that single classes never have. 10/10 will be coming back :)
author: Marianna Torres

text: I love the community you are creating. I really enjoy the series. It’s amazing to see how much I’ve learned from the first class. Thanks for putting so much time and energy into this!
author: Meghan

text: I used to forget little things constantly ever since I was young. I didn’t engage in a lot of mentally stimulating physical activities or physical exercise, especially when I reached high school. Then I met Michelle, who is a dancer and the founder of QLDSD, and naturally she convinced me to learn. Michelle started teaching me to dance, and I was resistant for years. Anytime I tried to dance, it was difficult to recall the patterns, and I couldn’t quite make my limbs move how I wanted. So it took a lot of convincing to be more consistent. Being more consistent with learning how to dance I realize that it improved my memory! My body feels healthier and I'm not tired all the time. Before, I didn’t care much about dance, but now I recommend dance to everyone, more importantly to those who say they can’t dance or have never danced before. Whatever excuse you tell others or yourself, it’s always a great decision to learn to dance in a safe space. I’m more excited than ever to be around queer folks and learn more from my partner and other instructors out there. Michelle is a patient teacher and a passionate dancer. Learning dance from her has improved a lot of areas in my life!
author: Pat P.

text: I've been taking bachata series with @queerlatindancesd and I highly recommend. In the Latin dance community the gender roles are so strict and if you don't fit within that role it can be highly discouraging. Not to mention there is not a lot of room for self expression. These classes are breaking that mold and making such a warm and welcoming space for all individuals. Cannot say enough good things about the series.
author: Keyra Ann Fallon
